notes.title: New Music Preview – The Sounds of the In-Between
notes.content:
What are the sounds that can be found within a liminal space? The soft shuffle of shoes on a shag carpet or the hum of fluorescent lights? Or might there be something less... mundane?

In Liminal Shroud, sound is more than background noise—it's a part of the experience. While wandering these shifting halls, you’ll encounter an eerie blend of isolation and presence. Curiosity will trade places with dread. Every note in the soundscape is designed to bring you deeper into the mystery.

Here's a glimpse of that experience in the video below, let the sounds drift in, and slip into the unsettling world of Liminal Shroud.

[previewyoutube=oHplRU_GPg4;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Noclipping in Liminal Shroud
notes.content:
[b]Noclipping[/b] is a part of reality in the backrooms, and is typically how one gets stuck there. However this anomaly can be useful, especially if you've taken the wrong path. 

Exploring Liminal Shroud will often give you different paths to take. Some will lead to progress, while others lead you astray. How do you explore a level full of slides that constantly send you deeper? 

Navigating a maze of slides can be tricky! But this place won't let you leave... until you figure it out.  If you take the wrong path, there should be a way back... even if it's one-way.

Let's take a look at one possible path through this oppressive concrete brutalist environment, and see what noclipping looks like!

[previewyoutube=FCZn_a4r8Po;full][/previewyoutube]


Creating these environments is an exercise in feeling out vibes. I often put audio in very early to try to figure out the "character" of the environment and help inform the visuals. Materials are very important for making liminal spaces feel believable, and I've spent some time refining the Glass Block shader. 

     [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45300888/49ed872d8f9ffd25a0b543e98e1c4188c756f71a.gif[/img]     

Remember glass block decor from the 80's/90's? Of course you do - it was tucked away in that dusty corner of your memory. 


In this level, I needed to create a way for you to start again from the top. Since there are many slide routes you can take, chances are you'll hit a dead end and have to noclip to the beginning to try a different route. The level will have certain spots where you can do this, and they may not always lead to a second chance!

     [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45300888/308e87b5d6ec761a3ed3071ed43fcf3684523c52.gif[/img]

notes.title: Development Update Sliding in!
notes.content:
[b]Greetings explorers! [/b]

I'm working on a new level featuring the slide system I've been developing. This will give you a choice for which path you want to take through the level. Which one is the correct path? Would you get on a slide that leads into the dark void where you can't see the end?

Below is a small preview of the slides and how they work. I have much of the level to build out and connect with slides, and different slides will take you on completely different paths through the level.

[previewyoutube=8a-VPmdY2b0;full][/previewyoutube]

As with previous levels, this will offer a navigation challenge for you to solve. Looking for clues in the environment and listening carefully will be the key to escape!

Cheers!
-M
